action: Review which third-party providers and cloud systems hold your data, limit what their accounts can search and export, and delete data you no longer need. Report incidents to the HKCERT hotline on (852) 8105 6060.
exec: Hong Kong's CERT says recent breaches at a travel firm, a university and a retail group show third-party and cloud systems are entry points for large data leaks.
plain: Hong Kong's cyber emergency team warns that several recent data leaks at local organisations show that data held by third-party providers and cloud services is at risk. It asks organisations to hold less data and limit access to it.

key_findings: HKCERT cites recent incidents in travel, education and retail: unauthorised access to the back-end system of EGL Tours' third-party IT provider, a Hong Kong Metropolitan University incident that may have involved about 5,000 people, and an A.S. Watson Group incident involving a third-party supplier.
It says there is currently no information that the incidents resulted from the same attack method.

It urges collecting and keeping only required data, restricting account, system and provider access to data (least privilege, with care over bulk export), and proportionate safeguards such as encryption.
recommendations: Collect and retain only necessary data and delete or anonymise the rest.
Restrict data access permissions for accounts, systems and third-party providers.
Apply safeguards in proportion to data sensitivity, including encryption at rest and in transit.

sources.name: HKCERT: Series of Cybersecurity Incidents Affecting Hong Kong Organisations
The Standard: Hong Kong Metropolitan University reports data breach affecting 5,000 people

summary: Hong Kong's CERT (HKCERT) issued a warning after recent data incidents at EGL Tours' IT provider, Hong Kong Metropolitan University (about 5,000 people possibly involved) and A.S. Watson Group (via a third-party supplier). It says no information links them to one attack method, and urges less data retention, least-privilege access and encryption.
title: HKCERT warns of Hong Kong data leaks via third-party and cloud systems

validation.note: HKCERT's own advisory read in full; The Standard read for the HKMU incident (discovered 4 Nov, about 5,000 people, reported to police and the privacy commissioner). EGL Tours and A.S. Watson details not read at their own sources.

review.note: Three incidents, 5,000 figure, no-common-method statement against HKCERT and The Standard
